draft.title: Types of joints
card: A joint is where two or more bones meet. Joints are grouped by how much movement they allow, which depends on the tissue that holds the bones together.
Fibrous
bones are joined by tough fibrous tissue and do not move. The joints between the bones of the skull are an example.
Cartilaginous
bones are joined by cartilage and move only slightly. The joints between the vertebrae of the spine are an example.
Synovial
bones meet in a fluid-filled space and move freely. The knee and the shoulder are examples.
draft.remember: The more tissue binds the bones, the less they move: fibrous none, cartilaginous slight, synovial free.

a.q: Which joint type lets the bones move only a small amount?
opts: Cartilaginous
Fibrous
Synovial
Skeletal
a.why: Cartilaginous joints join bones with cartilage, which allows slight movement. Fibrous joints are the tempting wrong choice, because they hold bones firmly and allow no movement at all.
a.clue: Think of the spine, where each vertebra moves a little.

b.q: Jess is a netballer. Which of her joints allows no movement at all?
opts: A joint between two bones of her skull
A joint between two vertebrae in her back
Her knee joint as she jumps
Her shoulder joint as she shoots
b.why: Joints in the skull are fibrous, so the bones are held firmly and do not move. The joints between vertebrae are the tempting wrong choice, because they are cartilaginous and allow slight movement.
b.clue: Which joint holds bones firmly together with tough fibrous tissue?

b.best: A joint between two bones of her skull

problems.detail: The remember line gives a rule the card does not teach: that the amount of tissue binding the bones decides movement. The card says movement depends on the type of tissue (fibrous tissue, cartilage, or a fluid-filled space). The 'more tissue, less movement' rule is also doubtful, because synovial joints are held by capsules and ligaments. Better: 'The tissue joining the bones sets how much they move: fibrous none, cartilaginous slight, synovial free.'

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card. The remember line adds a 'more tissue, less movement' rule the card does not teach and which is doubtful, so it should be reworded to refer to the type of tissue.
